shortDescription: Chicago Board of Trade wheat futures rose amid escalating conflict in the region, which was underlined by a morning attack on Dnipro, Ukraine, that hit a Bunge facility.

children: Chicago Board of Trade wheat futures rose amid escalating conflict in the region, which was underlined by a morning attack on Dnipro, Ukraine, that hit a Bunge facility.
Tit-for-tat attacks between Ukraine and Russia have choked off grain exports from the region.

Both Ukraine and Russia have stepped up attacks in recent weeks against commercial ships, sending world grain prices higher. Russia has previously rejected the idea of a ceasefire in the Black Sea as a "half-measure".
Diplomatic efforts to end Russia's war with Ukraine encouraged profit-taking earlier in the session.

"Renewed Russian comments about restarting U.S.-mediated peace talks gave funds an excuse to trim risk, while tomorrow’s (USDA) report adds another reason not to chase prices before seeing the new numbers," CM Navigator analysts wrote.

Expana raised its outlook for European Union soft wheat exports this season as reduced Black Sea shipments shifted demand to the bloc, while cutting its EU maize harvest forecast to a 34-year low after late-season heat and dryness damaged crops.

The commodity data firm put EU soft wheat exports in 2026/27 at 29.5 million metric tons, up from 28.7 million tons projected in August, while lowering its estimate for 2025/26 shipments to 28.5 million tons.
CBOT December soft red winter wheat (WZ26) settled 12-1/2 cents higher to $7.41-1/4 per bushel.
Kansas City December hard red winter wheat (KWZ26) settled 12-1/2 cents higher to $8.18-3/4 per bushel.
Minneapolis December wheat (MWEZ26) settled 14-1/2 cents higher to $7.62-1/2 per bushel.
